criteria.description: Correctly differentiates the left side, getting lambda*e^{lambda t}*v.
Correctly computes the right side, getting e^{lambda t}*(Av).
Correctly divides out e^{lambda t} to arrive at Av=lambda*v.

solutions.fullSolution:
xdot(t) = d/dt[e^{lambda t} v] = lambda*e^{lambda t}*v (v constant, differentiate the scalar exponential).
A*x(t) = A(e^{lambda t} v) = e^{lambda t}(Av) (linearity of matrix-vector multiplication, scalar factors out).
Setting these equal (required for the ansatz to solve xdot=Ax): lambda*e^{lambda t}*v = e^{lambda t}*(Av). Since e^{lambda t} is never zero, divide both sides by it: lambda*v = Av, i.e. Av=lambda*v, the eigenvector/eigenvalue equation.
x1(1) = 2*e^-1 + e^-3 = 2*0.367879 + 0.049787 = 0.735759+0.049787 = 0.785546, rounds to 0.786. (Verified with NumPy while authoring this module.)

criteria.description: Correctly identifies asymptotic stability from the negative real part.
Correctly computes the oscillation period from the imaginary part.
Correctly describes the trajectory as a decaying/stable spiral.

solutions.fullSolution: Real part -0.5 < 0: asymptotically stable, solutions decay with envelope e^{-0.5t}. Imaginary part 2: oscillation at angular frequency 2, period T=2*pi/2=pi. The trajectory spirals inward toward the origin, completing a full rotation roughly every pi time units while shrinking by a factor e^{-0.5} per unit time: a stable spiral.

criteria.description: Correctly reads off the eigenvalues 1 and -2 from the diagonal matrix.
Correctly concludes the system is unstable overall (any positive eigenvalue).
Correctly names this a saddle, describing the mixed stable/unstable directions.

solutions.fullSolution: Eigenvalues (diagonal entries): lambda1=1, lambda2=-2. Since lambda1>0, the system is unstable overall: generic initial conditions grow without bound along the lambda1=1 eigendirection (the x1-axis). Real eigenvalues of opposite sign: this is a saddle, attracting along the x2-axis (lambda2=-2) but repelling along the x1-axis (lambda1=1).
